subsystems.name: Accelerator chip
subsystems.role: does the matrix maths that runs a language model.

subsystems.name: Unified memory
subsystems.role: must hold the whole model, so capacity matters more than raw speed here.

subsystems.name: Storage
subsystems.role: keeps model weights, which can be 20–200 GB each, on hand.

subsystems.name: Host and interconnect
subsystems.role: runs the operating system and links one node to another.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal
subsystems.role: fits a 100–300 W chip into something that sits on a desk quietly.

subsystems.role: quantises the model and serves requests.
parts: runtime such as llama.cpp or vLLM
4-bit formats such as GPTQ, AWQ or GGUF

buildSteps.title: Design the chip
buildSteps.detail: Engineers lay out tensor cores, memory controllers and caches, then verify the design in simulation before committing it to silicon.

buildSteps.title: Fab the wafer
buildSteps.detail: The chip is made on a leading-edge logic process — for the fastest parts, at 3–4 nm class nodes.

buildSteps.title: Package the memory
buildSteps.detail: Memory is soldered onto the same package as the chip (LPDDR) or stacked on an interposer (HBM), giving very wide short traces.

buildSteps.title: Make the board
buildSteps.detail: The package is mounted on a small motherboard with voltage regulators, PCIe lanes, an SSD socket and network ports.

buildSteps.title: Solve the thermal problem
buildSteps.detail: A vapour chamber and blower are tuned so the chip can run sustained inference without throttling or sounding like a server.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and burn in
buildSteps.detail: Machines are built, run under load for hours and checked for memory errors before shipping.

buildSteps.title: Install the stack
buildSteps.detail: Firmware, drivers and an inference runtime are flashed, and the operator downloads quantised model weights.

buildSteps.title: Quantise and serve
buildSteps.detail: Weights are compressed from 16-bit to 4-bit, which roughly quarters memory use at some cost in quality, then the model is loaded and benchmarked in tokens per second.

prerequisites.why: putting many gigabytes of memory on the same package is what lets a small box hold a large model.
4-bit formats shrink models enough for one machine to hold them.
keeps memory from ballooning as conversation context grows.
linking several nodes into one bigger model needs bandwidth that consumer ports only partly deliver.
unified memory above 128 GB is still expensive, which limits which models can run locally.
